notes:
Background: Quantum Helix is building low-latency conversational features for institutional trading desks + live transcription for trader voice channels. They require Dedicated capacity with strict residency and audit controls.

Main asks (summary):
- Clear latency SLOs across percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for both non-streaming API calls (batch/generate) and streaming token-level responses.
- Definition alignment: customer currently measures "client-side end-to-end" (SDK + network) but wants Redwood to propose server-side "service" SLO + e2e budget split.
- Throughput guarantees: plan for reserved GPUs to handle peak of ~1,200 concurrent streams + 12k non-streaming qps with fallbacks.
- SLA negotiation points: financial credits tied to p99 miss-rate, minimum throughput availability, and scheduled maintenance windows.

Latency specifics discussed on 2026-02-18:
- Non-streaming endpoints (document summarization, rerank): customer target p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms for 2k token requests. Redwood proposed baseline server-side SLO p50 80ms / p95 300ms / p99 600ms measured at server ingress-to-last-token-complete. Recommendation: add 25-40ms client/network budget to produce e2e targets.
- Streaming endpoints (chat & transcription): customer wants token-level responsiveness. They requested token p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 500ms. Redwood recommended measuring both: (a) first-byte latency for start-of-stream, (b) inter-token latency distribution for steady-state. Proposed tokenization: measure per-token latency at server emission timestamp; provide percentiles over moving 1h windows.
- Measurement alignment: agreed approach = canonicalize metrics into two sets: "service SLOs" (server-side timings via agent/ingress logs) + "observed e2e" (client SDK telemetry). Action: Redwood SE to provide instrumentation snippet for client-side SDK to correlate traces (trace-id preserved).
- P99 budgeting model: propose soft SLOs for streaming (grace period and adaptive batching) + hard SLOs for mission-critical non-streaming endpoints. For billing/SLA triggers, use server-side p99 measured over daily windows with 5m rolling checks and a threshold of 0.1% violations before crediting.

POC design notes:
- Load shape: replay real production traffic (sanitized) + synthetic spikes to 1.5x expected peak.
- Metrics to capture: server-ingress-to-last-token, server-first-byte, inter-token-mean & tail, client-received-first-byte, qps, concurrency, GPU utl, batch-size distribution.
- Acceptance criteria: sustained p95 and p99 within agreed budgets for 48h under 1.2x peak, no GPU OOM, fallback latency < double baseline.

- Legal to finalize data residency and retention terms in Addendum A.
- Agree on SLA credit schedule (monthly windows vs per-incident).
